answer: Yes. The story uses sustained metaphors to deepen its portrayal of insecurity and self-presentation. Quentin’s apparent superiority becomes a “fixed geography,” while his collapsing verbal defenses resemble “a little ruined shed.” The recurring blue ink ultimately symbolizes his carefully controlled way of processing vulnerability. Corporate idioms such as “pivot” and “mutual realignment of expectations” also reveal how he uses polished language to avoid admitting failure.
